task: Fix the missing audit entries after the async audit writer was changed to a fire-and-forget pattern.

candidate_memories.content: Audit log has gaps for 3% of requests since the audit writer was changed to fire-and-forget async.
The audit writer must use an async pattern with a durable buffer and confirmed writes, not fire-and-forget.
The change to fire-and-forget was made to reduce latency but was not reviewed against the audit completeness requirement.
Audit writers must guarantee durability; latency optimizations must not reduce write guarantees.
The 3% gap corresponds to requests where the audit write goroutine was preempted before the write completed.
The audit log is stored in an append-only PostgreSQL table with a write-ahead log enabled.
Session 4 note: the compliance team requested audit log retention to be extended from 7 years to 10 years.
Old practice: audit writes were synchronous before the latency reduction initiative.
The audit log is replicated to a separate archive store every night for compliance backup.
Session 10 note: the audit team added a dashboard for audit log coverage rate.
Old audit guide: the audit writer used a synchronous write with a 500ms timeout.
Audit systems must use durable write patterns; fire-and-forget is only appropriate for non-critical telemetry.
Session 7 note: the security team added field-level encryption for sensitive audit log entries.
The audit log table is partitioned by month; each partition is purged after the retention period expires.
A compliance audit in session 3 showed 100% audit coverage for all request types.
The audit write path uses a separate database connection pool to avoid contention with the application.
Latency improvements in audit paths must be validated against audit completeness guarantees before deploying.
Session 11 note: the legal team approved the current audit log schema for court admissibility.
Old async design: a channel-based audit writer was prototyped but rejected due to memory concerns.
The audit API allows compliance officers to query logs by user, action, resource, and time range.
